The false positive is fixed and committed as `2855dfa` on `main`.

**Cause:** `stages_all()` in `src/staging.py` reads `git commit -m"add export handler"` as the single word `-madd export handler`. It treated any short-option cluster as flags, so the letter `a` inside the message text matched `-a` ("stage everything"). `git commit -ma x` was also wrongly flagged.

**Fix:** A short-option cluster now stops at the first option that takes a value (`m`, `F`, `c`, `C`, `t`, `u`, `S`), since the rest of the word is that value. I added tests for the message case and for `-ma`. The tests also confirm that `-am`, `-a -m x`, `git add -A` and `git add .` still get flagged.

**Verification:** I reproduced the bug first (the message case returned `True`). After the fix, the edge-case checks and `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` both pass.

**What I committed:** only `src/staging.py` and `tests/test_staging.py`. I left out your uncommitted README note and the untracked `notes/` folder.

**Limitation:** I couldn't read your global Claude settings, so I couldn't confirm which hook fires the reminder. The reminder is the `stages_all` check that the README describes, and this fix addresses it. If the warning still shows after this change, the hook is probably running an older copy of the script, or it is matching the command text separately.
